reviews.text: Saved My Skin. For years I never knew what to put on my skin. There’s thousands of products, hundreds of different skin types and combinations, dermatologists are expensive, skinfluencers can lie and promote scams, and it can be so daunting you don’t even know where to start. I finally caved and got the app and it helped SO MUCH to find products that work for me. I have fungal acne, psoriasis, and sensitive skin. Please Try!. OVERVIEW: Great app: includes ingredient breakdowns, skincare tailored towards specific concerns, and product dupes based on pricing and ingredients. 
I go through an obscene amount of sifting through product reviews to search for the perfect fit for my skin routine. On a whim, I thought I’d try a free trial of this app. I’m really bad at canceling subscriptions, but didn’t cancel and paid for the full year (there’s a subscription refund available) and decided to keep perusing SkinSort. What I’ve found is a really kind, and articulate little skincare community. Lately, I’ve been really wrapped up in building reviews as well as commenting on others’ reviews too. What I wish for this app moving forward is that reviews remain unbiased and NOT incentivized. I’ve been influenced enough and I just want honest reviews. Full disclosure: I have NOT been paid to write this. Happy skincare journey!

Can be misleading. Overall it’s a cool aggregator of information, but it can present it in a really misleading way especially in the personalized scoring feature. As someone with extremely sensitive skin, this tool seemed initially a godsend, but when I tried using products that scored 90%+ for me, the results were horrible. My skin was burning and inflamed when using a popular product the app recommended to me. When instead I used a product that scored in the red < 50% for suitability, my skin felt much better. For laymen like me, I think it’s best to use this app just to check for ingredients, but don’t follow its advice. Save your money for a dermatologist.

Overpriced Search Engine. I really wanted to like SkinSort, but it ended up being a disappointment. The app feels like a stripped-down search engine. It’s less useful than just looking things up on Google or even browsing Reddit, where you get a wider range of users’ experiences and opinions.

One of the biggest issues is how misleading it is about creating a “routine.” That feature is either extremely limited or just not actually functional in a meaningful way. I expected something personalized and helpful, but it didn’t deliver.

There’s also no consideration for budget when suggesting products, which makes the recommendations feel out of touch and impractical. For something that’s paid, I expected a lot more value and usability.

Overall, it feels overpriced for what it offers, and I honestly regret paying for it. I wish I could get a refund.

Must Have Skincare App!. A lifelong devotee to skincare products, I’ve found this app to be indispensable. Most helpful is the ability to enter in a product name or scan the package and/or ingredient list and instantly see a numbered rating as to compatibility with my individual skin type and needs. Not only does SkinSort provide an objective rating, it individually lists all ingredients along with their intended purpose and a detailed description of how my skin may react to a specific ingredient. Products/preferences can be sorted and stored based upon an extensive list of criteria such as fragrance free, reef safe, paraben free, etc. I am already fairly knowledgeable about the most common active skincare ingredients, but there are hundreds of others I know nothing about, SkinSort has been incredibly helpful and informative. I just spent 3 hours in Marshall’s scanning products for compatibility & I can already say SkinSort has saved me $$$ by steering me away from products that could be problematic for my skin despite the product label advertising a seemingly perfect match! The shelf section is quite helpful in that you can easily customize specific “shelves” to maintain organized lists such as product wishlists, products I own, products rated a perfect match, etc. The diary section is incredibly helpful for tracking one’s current skin health/symptoms, reactions to products and environmental conditions, and gauging the effectiveness of specific products over time. One can create and store multi step routines to keep track of and adjust based on skincare response. The only feature of the app I urge caution with is the area where users can subjectively review products with a 1-5 star rating based upon their experience. As each person’s skin type/needs, product tolerance, proficiency/experience with active ingredients, fragrance/texture preference, etc. is different, it’s important to take the information provided in these reviews with a grain of salt. One can absolutely adore a product only to despise it months later. I’ve read scathing 1 star reviews on products MY skin thrives on and vice versa. Finally, the one time I submitted a question regarding functionality of a specific feature to SkinSort, they were incredibly prompt with their helpful and informative response. In summary, this app is a MUST HAVE for experienced skincare enthusiasts and beginners alike. Whomever created this incredibly comprehensive APP did it BIG ❤️

Charged me $76.35 immediately after agreeing to 7-day FREE trial. I would love to actually review the app and its utility, but I’m too frustrated to even look at it now. I thought the tool looked like it might be helpful to me, and am totally up for paying for things I use… However, immediately - less than 10 seconds after clicking my side button for approval - after agreeing to the offered 7-day FREE TRIAL (via the app), I received a notification that I had been charged $76.35. There wasn’t even time for me to cancel the subscription if I wanted to! I provided feedback via their portal (promoted after install), but when I attempted to use their “contact us” page and selected “request a refund” (or similar), I was directed to contact Apple services. I understand how the contracts work (that Apple is responsible for reversing charges), but it’s super frustrating to have to do such legwork in the first place. When I requested a refund from Apple, there wasn’t a text field where I could alert them that I was charged immediately instead of after the 7-day free trial (part of which which included a promised reminder email two days before renewal. 🙄)

Users shouldn’t have to be leery about signing up for free trials. It’s one thing for users to complain because they weren’t aware of the T&C (ex: being charged at end of trial unless they cancel 24 hours beforehand) - that’s annoying. It’s another thing when the user is mindful of what they’re signing up for and the terms associated, and those terms are breached seconds after they agreed to them.

The App That Makes Exploring Skincare A Smooth Experience. I’ve only started using the SkinSort since the beginning of the year but this is truly something I wish existed when I first got into skincare. I love it even more now that there is a mobile app especially when I need to scan a product I’m curious about in person. There’s so many useful features in the in regards to comparing products, researching ingredients, a routine/diary tracker, finding cheaper dupes and an extensive database. And the best thing is that it’s all free! There are some additional perks with the subscription but I wouldn’t say that’s required to fully obtain all the great insight and benefits that this app has to offer. One of my favorite things about the app is how clear and organized the ingredient breakdown for each product is. The symbols for the ingredient help you clearly indicate the main traits to know for it which are very useful for detecting potential irritants. I also am a fan of how each review by users is very authentic which is something that I feel similar apps are lacking. If you’re someone who feels easily overwhelmed by not knowing where to start, they also offer helpful blogs that breakdown the need to know essentials. Wether you’re starting out or you’re a skincare junkie, SkinSort should be your first choice! Kudos to the developers they’ve done an awesome job with this app and , I really hope they keep up the good work!!!

FINALLY AN APP!!. i’ve been using skinsort for so long (maybe like a year), when i first discovered it- IT WAS LIKE AN ANGEL THAT DESCENDED FROM THE HEAVENS AND GAVE ME THIS GLORIOUS WEBSITE/(now)APP. it’s helped me be more decisive and picky with the products i buy. especially when it breaks down the ingredients, and how people in the community feel about them. key features i love: 1. comparing products if you’re feeling conflicted with buying one product verses the other, YOU CAN COMPARE THEM. when i tell you i tried looking for other apps/websites that did this, i came up with nothing. how i felt about this is, “how hard is it to make something to compare products”. not hard because skinsort has that feature for you! 😁 2. searching tool you can filter things down, this is probably like the most simple thing but they i believe they’re more detailed with their search tool. you can search based on: COUNTRY, INGREDIENTS, PREFERENCES, CATEGORY, and so much more. 3. UPLOADING PRODUCTS if they don’t have a product, AND YOU HAVE IT. upload it. that’s it, you can just upload it, they’ll double check everything and the information. like this app/website is so perfect. they check the ingredients as well, and i feel like that shows how much hard work each person who works at skinsort does. 4. for you, holy grails, trending, and more buttons now this is new and i personally love it, because i get confused easily on what is doing wHAT. so the fact that they have an oil control option is nice, because searching yourself can be really difficult. especially if you’re new to skincare and trying to understand everything/looking for things for your SKIN. 5. skin care diary now i personally don’t use this, because i just have a hard time with logging things in 😭, but it’s really helpful for other people who are set on keeping track on their skincare. especially if you’re forgetful, and if you forgot what routine you used on what. and what broke you out on what day when you used a certain routine, yk? 6. you can FOLLOW PEOPLE? i feel like this is a good feature especially for really big skincare lovers who like to review for other people because it does do us all a service. we know how it affects someone, and it better helps us judge something based on other people’s experience. 7. SCANNING. when i tell you, it’s hard to walk into let’s say MARSHALLS. and be in the aisle trying to look up a product, COPY and PASTE the ingredients into the checker. now, we have the camera to scan, round of applause- because skinsort made it easier for all of us. there’s more to skinsort, but for someone who’s struggled with their skin and got into skincare trying to look for solutions. and couldn’t come up with any product that helped with hyperpigmentation in the past. i’m glad there are more companies and PEOPLE who are digging deep to understand skin better. and that are there to build a big and more effective community around skincare. this means a lot to someone who didn’t know anything at first, and now knows how to help others with their skin. for people getting into skincare, please use this app- it’ll save you the struggle and time of researching on google and going from website to website trying to understand ingredients (there are some ingredients on this website even skinsort doesn’t know but there are people who are taking time to figure it out and post onto there) and how products will affect skin. and thank you skinsort for making life so much easier when it comes to skincare.

I deducted one star as I don’t LOVE the scoring system, I’ve noticed scores for products going up if I say that I like an ingredient that’s in it, instead of the score purely being off of the compatibility of the product & my skin - you can’t completely rely on scores from apps as like I said earlier you have to take into account different variables that aren’t necessarily processed by the scoring system.
